assertions.name: against_the_PEAK_the_required_factor_is_within_a_quarter_percent_of_three
assertions.note: a law with no surface/Coulomb/asymmetry/pairing term is a pure volume term, so the peak is the honest comparison -- against the median it is 7.3 % off, and that difference IS the missing terms

assertions.name: the_peak_of_B_over_A_is_at_the_iron_peak
assertions.note: A = 62, which is where the ratio ceiling of 3.00-3.01 was measured on 2026-09-04 -- the ceiling and this factor are one observation

assertions.name: the_multiplicity_parameter_does_not_supply_a_factor_of_three
assertions.note: 0.335 / 0.984 / 1.709 -- non-uniform and nowhere near 3, and the p-p bond gets WEAKER

assertions.name: at_m_equals_two_two_letters_give_a_NEGATIVE_bond_energy
assertions.note: ['pp', 'pn'] have b > 1 at m=2, so `m` is not a multiplicity of bond strength at all -- whatever supplies the factor, it is not this parameter

assertions.name: disjoint_tripling_lands_within_one_percent_of_the_peak
assertions.note: 0.25 % below. But see the two assumptions: disjoint-support factorisation of tr_M is ASSUMED not verified, and the 3A layout cannot express a colour tube -- colour-matched pairs across an interface are distance 3 apart, needing a braid rather than the single generator sigma_{3k+2} the word emits

assertions.name: a_constant_cannot_change_the_spread_only_the_median
assertions.note: identical to every digit -- so the median moving to 0.895 (10.5 % over-bound) is the expected signature of a pure volume term, not evidence FOR the factor. It is the absence of evidence against it
